comment: Lots of reading, some easy and interesting, most not. A tough grader on the two in-person essays and his handwriting was so small I couldn't even read what I did wrong. But he's knowledgeable, passionate and self-aware, and that's good enough for me.

This class had so many readings and your grade is basically based off of how much you participate in class. The readings can be very hard to understand and then you have debates based off of them. Dr. Bischof is also a hard grading when it comes to papers. I would not take this class.

So much reading and tough grader, but he will make you a better writer. He expects a lot from his students. 4 grades each worth 25% for the entire semester: participation and 3 papers. Be ready to speak and do 50+ page readings.

Organized around debates about things like Luddites and Quaker gunmakers and making tea.  Learned a lot of surprising things.  Enjoyed the debates.  Two pretty standard essays and then a final essay about an object you choose related to tea advertising or consumption or growing.  A lot of reading, some hard, some easier, mostly kind of interesting.

Dr. Bischof is a good professor but his class is awful. He gives out 60+ page readings for homework and good luck understanding them. His class is 100% discussion based and it's clear if you didn't read. He gives out "short writes" which are basically pop quizzes if you read or not. And the essay topics are so difficult. Don't take this.

Dr. Bischof was a great professor and one of my favorites I've had at UR thus far. He's really knowledgeable and passionate about the subject matter. He is a fair grader, but on essays especially will push you to do your best (2 ~2,000 word essays). Readings are manageable and though midterm and final cover a lot of ground, he's very helpful.

Enthusiastic. Wants you to understand readings when discussing. Will help by building on student comments. Could do more to help students talk to each other not just him in discussion. Likes to write on board a lot during discussions. Grading about average, not too hard or too easy. Good prof on whole.

LOVE THIS MAN. Amazingly brilliant & well-versed in what he teaches. Go to his office hours to discuss the papers (I had 3) , & listen to his advice. Participate. Hes energetic & makes it easy to speak in class if you are plain shy or hesitant. I took Modern Cities with him & it still is my fav history class Ive taken (and Im a history minor)
Super knowledgeable about british history and really excited to share it. Discussions can be great and we had fairly long ones pretty much every class.
Young and enthusiastic.  Serious, but nice also ultimately.  Sometimes class drags, but then sometimes out of nowhere it gets really interesting.  you must read and work hard on your essays though.

Clearly knows his stuff and get really excited when he is teaching sometimes.  Covers a longer period of time than other history courses, which is a nice change of pace.   Sincere.  Will help you if you ask.

I got pretty interested in it. My friend too. A few did not. He's enthusiastic though and will keep you engaged if you want to be engaged. On papers will help you IF you work to help yourself.  It was hard, but satisfying to see my paper grades improve. I write better now. Will take another class with him if my schedule allows.
Seems to think very highly of himself. Doesn't know how to give purpose to the class and the readings for those who aren't interested in history. Readings are dense, long, and boring.

Reading load isn't terrible but you have to do it all and some of it is hard.  Discussions are based on readings and they can be good.  You spend a while figuring out together what the reading said, which is really helpful.  Then you discuss more broadly.  Some lecturing most classes.  Not hard to get a low B, but really hard to get an A.

Hard grader on written work, but worth taking.  Good class topics that start out fairly interesting and get even more interesting later in the semester.  Great discussions.  But you have to read for pretty much every class and you have to really work on your essays if you want to do good.  He expects a lot from you.
